title: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi
summary: Lakshmi Bai, born Manikarnika around 1827, married the maharaja of Jhansi in 1842. The East India Company annexed Jhansi under the doctrine of lapse after his death, and she refused to give it up. She defended it against General Hugh Rose in March 1858 and died fighting the British near Gwalior in June 1858.

uncertainty.note: Birth year is given as "around 1827"; death is June 1858, with the day given as 18 June by one source and not stated by the other.

where.modern_name: Jhansi Fort, Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, India (pin is Jhansi, the place of her rule and siege; she died near Gwalior)
where.historical_name: Jhansi, a princely state annexed by the East India Company

importance.justification: A leading figure of the 1857 rebellion, remembered as a symbol of resistance to the East India Company.

sources.title: Lakshmi Bai, India's warrior queen who fought the British
June 18 1858: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi Dies While Fighting the British Troops near Gwalior

reviewer_note: Birth year differs: National Geographic says around 1827, Maps of India says 19 November 1828; National Geographic notes history and myth are intertwined and gives no exact death date, so the 18 June date rests on one popular page. Britannica could not be opened.
